 ---- Petitioner  Versus  1. State Of Chhattisgarh Through Station House Officer P.S. Mahila  Thana, Bilaspur District Bilaspur Chhattisgarh  2. Smt. Archana Shrivastava D/o Late Shri Ratneshwar Shrivastava Aged  About 36 Years R/o Quarter No. B-169, Ramagreen City, Sarkanda P.S.
 Sarkanda, Tehsil And District Bilaspur Chhattisgarh  ---- Respondent For Petitioner : Shri Prateek Singh Thakur, Advocate.
For Respondent/State : Ms. M. Asha, Panel Lawyer.
For Respondent No.2. : Shri Awadhesh Mishra, Advocate.
Hon'ble
Shri Deepak Kumar Tiwari, J Order On Board 20/02/2023 :

1. The present petition has been preferred by the petitioners seeking to quash the impugned order dated 22.9.2022 passed by the Judicial Magistrate 1st Class,
Bilaspur in Criminal Case No.425/2017 for offence under Section 498A/34 of the IPC.
2. Facts of the case are that petitioner No.1 was married with respondent No.2 on 24.11.2012 at Renukut, District Sonbhadra, (UP).
After few years of marriage, dispute occurred between the parties and in spite of social meetings, the matter could not be settled.

A divorce petition has been filed by petitioner No.1 before the Family Court,
Ankit Shrivastava vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122328081/
1 Sonbhadra (UP) and on 15.7.2022, a decree of divorce was passed by the family Court.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thereafter, respondent No.2 moved an application for maintenance under Section 125 of the CrPC and in the said proceeding, the family Court awarded Rs.3500/- as maintenance to respondent No.2.

In the year 2016, a complaint was also made by respondent No.2 against her husband and his parents and on the basis of said complaint, a criminal case was registered under Section 498-A of the IPC vide Crime No.3/2016, and charge sheet was also filed before the JMFC, Bilaspur, which is pending.
During the pendency of the criminal case the parties had settled their dispute by entering into an agreement dated 16.9.2022.
Under the said agreement, certain amount was agreed to be paid by the petitioners to respondent No.2, in lieu of which the criminal case was agreed to be withdrawn by the respondent-wife.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that both the parties have settled their dispute amicably by way of compromise.

4. The Additional Registrar (Judicial) of this Court has recorded the statement of the parties in which they have categorically supported the aforesaid compromise which was arrived on their own free will, without any undue influence, coercion or inducement.
So, further continuation of the criminal proceeding would not serve any purpose.

5. It is well settled that the High Court in exercise of its inherent powers can quash criminal proceedings or FIR or complaint and Section 320 of the Code does not limit or affect the powers under Sections 482 of the Code.

{See : B.S. Joshi and Others Vs. State of Haryana and Another,
(2003) 4 SCC 675}.
6.

sentences.text: In view of the above, the Petition is allowed and the impugned order dated 22.9.2022 passed by the JMFC, Bilaspur and the criminal proceeding initiated vide Criminal Case No.425/2017 pending before the said Court for offence under Section 498-A/34 of the IPC are hereby quashed.
